name: Nucleo-F411RE (official ST board)

button.note: Blue USER button B1, with an onboard pull-up; reads LOW when pressed. The black button is RESET

buses.i2c: I2C1: SCL PB8 (D15) / SDA PB9 (D14), the two pins at the top-right corner of the Arduino header
buses.spi: SPI1: SCK PA5 (D13) / MISO PA6 (D12) / MOSI PA7 (D11) / CS usually PB6 (D10). Note that SCK and the onboard LED share the same pin, PA5
buses.uart: Serial (USART2): TX PA2 / RX PA3, wired straight to the onboard ST-Link's USB virtual COM port; USART1: TX PA9 (D8) / RX PA10 (D2); USART6: TX PC6 (Morpho) / RX PC7 (D9)

power: 3.3V logic. On the F4 series the vast majority of I/O pins are 5V-tolerant (FT) in digital mode, but when configured as ADC analog inputs the limit is still 3.3V (verify). The board is powered over USB; the 5V header pin supplies about 300mA and the 3V3 pin about 300mA. You can also feed 7-12V into VIN
flash_how: Exactly like the F103RB: the top half of the board is a built-in ST-Link V2-1, and one mini-B USB cable to your computer handles flashing, power and serial; nothing else to buy. pio run -t upload flashes directly; LD1 blinks red/green while flashing. A USB drive named NODE_F411RE appears on your computer, and dragging a .bin onto it flashes too. pio device monitor for serial
gotchas: The onboard LED LD2 is on PA5 (D13), active-high. PA5 is also SPI1 SCK, so the LED flickers when you use SPI; that's normal
Unlike the F103, the F411's PA5 has a timer channel (TIM2_CH1), so analogWrite(PA5) does produce PWM and the onboard LED can do a breathing effect

D0/D1 (PA3/PA2) are disconnected by default (SB62/SB63 open) because USART2 goes to the ST-Link virtual COM port. Serial output over USB works fine, but there's no signal on the D0/D1 header pins (verify)
The USER button on PC13 reads LOW when pressed; pinMode(PC13, INPUT) is enough
The F411 has no DAC and no Ethernet/USB-host style peripherals; don't be misled by the 'F4' label. Its strengths are a high clock, lots of RAM and an FPU
There's only one ADC (ADC1), 12-bit, with fast enough sampling; but the Arduino header only exposes six channels A0-A5. More are on the Morpho headers (PC2, PC3, PC4, PC5, PB1)
A4/A5 (PC1/PC0) are not I2C pins; use D14/D15 for I2C
PC14/PC15 are taken by the 32.768kHz crystal and PC13 is the button; don't use these three as ordinary I/O
The USB port is mini-B, not the same as a phone cable
512KB Flash and 128KB RAM are plenty: U8g2 full-buffer mode plus a CJK font fit with room to spare, which is what makes this board more comfortable than the F103 series

left.name: IOREF
left.note: Wired to 3.3V; tells shields this board's logic level

left.name: A0 / PA0
left.note: Use this to read the potentiometer

right.name: AREF
right.note: ADC reference voltage; normally leave it alone

right.name: D13 / PA5
right.note: Onboard LED LD2, active-high; on the F411 it can do PWM breathing. Also the SPI clock

right.name: D8 / PA9
right.note: Connect to an external serial module's RX

right.name: D5 / PB4
right.note: JTAG isn't enabled by default on the F4; safe to use

right.name: D2 / PA10
right.note: Connect to an external serial module's TX

right.name: D1 / PA2
right.note: Taken by the ST-Link virtual COM port; no signal on the header pin by default (verify)

bottom.name: PC13
bottom.note: Blue USER button, LOW when pressed. On Morpho header CN7

bottom.name: PB12
bottom.note: Morpho only; good for buttons and relays

bottom.name: PA13
bottom.note: SWDIO, wired to the onboard ST-Link; leave it alone
